activities.anchor: a credentialed profession. Entry requires master's-level training
activities.caption: file the claims — art therapy or not?
activities.name: atpBorderBuckets

config.prompt: The definition's border patrol — file each claim:

items.label: a credentialed mental-health profession with its own methods and rules
supervised clinical hours and board certification (ATCB)
the artwork itself is confidential clinical material
art is nice for sad people
you must be good at drawing for it to work

config.why: The clinical work lives in the process of making — a scribble made honestly can carry more treatment than a polished drawing made defensively.

activities.caption: rebuild the founding story, sketchbook to profession
activities.name: atpFoundingOrder

config.prompt: Two continents, two instincts, thirty years — put the founding story in order:
items: Adrian Hill, convalescing from tuberculosis, coins 'art therapy' (c. 1942)
Naumburg develops dynamically oriented art therapy — the image as symbolic communication (1940s)
Kramer articulates art as therapy — the creative act strengthens the ego (1958)
Ulman founds the first professional journal, the Bulletin of Art Therapy (1961)
the British Association of Art Therapists (1964) and the American Art Therapy Association (1969) follow
config.why: The wartime-era roots — sanatoria, hospitals, disturbed children, later veterans — still shape where the profession works and whom it serves.

activities.caption: pair each tradition with its signature move
activities.name: atpTraditionsMatch

config.prompt: The theory families and their signature moves — pair them:

pairs.right: refuses interpretation from above — the client is the authority on their own image
'speak as the dark corner of this picture' — become the drawing
fear hierarchies for graded exposure, comic-strip futures for rehearsing coping
the image functions like a dream — a third party in the room

config.why: None of these displaced the founders; they layered options a therapist selects by client and goal.

activities.anchor: organises media and tasks along a processing ladder
activities.caption: pin the starting level on the ETC ladder
activities.name: atpETCPlace

config.prompt: Trauma-informed practice begins at which level of the Expressive Therapies Continuum?
config.why: The kinaesthetic–sensory level: traumatic memory is stored heavily in sensory and body channels and often resists verbal narration — 'speechless terror' — so begin where memory's format actually is.
config.context: The ladder climbs to perceptual–affective, then cognitive–symbolic, with an integrating creative level above — containment before exploration.

activities.anchor: the therapist is not decoding a secret dictionary
activities.caption: true or false — the symbol dictionary
activities.name: atpSymbolJudge

statements.s: A snake, a black scribble or an empty house mean nothing in general and very specific things in particular.
statements.why: Cross-cultural research dismantled the idea of universal signs — meaning depends on the individual, culture and context.

statements.s: Mid-century projective testing promised more certainty than symbols possess.
statements.why: Draw a house-tree-person, look up the fixed meanings — over-reach, now largely retired from interpretation-by-formula.

statements.s: Modern practice keeps the fixed symbol dictionary, just with better entries.
statements.why: No dictionary: the image is data about this person, read with cultural humility and co-constructed meaning.

statements.s: The process — hesitation, pressure, erasing — is read at least as attentively as the product.
statements.why: Process observation beats symbol lookup; the client's account of their own image outranks the therapist's hypothesis.

activities.anchor: Why should making pictures change people?
activities.caption: drag the divider — externalisation
activities.name: atpExternalCompare

config.prompt: Mechanism one of four — drag between before and after:

before.label: Inside the maker
before.text: A monstrous anxiety with no outside — nothing to look at, nothing to argue with, nothing to paint over.

after.label: On the paper
after.text: A feeling moved onto paper exists outside the maker — visible, at arm's length, discussable: that stance shift is the treatment.

config.why: With mastery and flow, sensory regulation, and symbolic expression — images hold contradiction a sentence would flatten.

activities.caption: run the third session — what goes on the table?
activities.name: atpSessionBranch

config.root: The ten-year-old from the house fire has drawn his blanket fort, named the dense corner 'the fire coming in', and added a door with a lock. Session three.

start.text: What do you put on the table?

choices.label: Keep firm coloured pencils indefinitely — it's working
Open straight to clay
choices.feedback: Clay invites confrontation — the deepest end.

choices.label: Move to paint, then clay as he holds more

stall.text: Containment without progression stalls: the media are supposed to open as the client's capacity grows — tracking growing ability to hold difficult material is part of the treatment.

clay.text: Clay invites confrontation — the least controllable, most confrontational end of the media spectrum, chosen only once regulation is established.

open.text: Across later sessions the media open up — paint, then clay — tracking his growing capacity to hold difficult material, documented against the intake goals.

config.why: Media choice is clinical choice: a watercolour wash and a fine technical pen differ like a sedative and a stimulant.

activities.anchor: From these mechanisms flow the practice decisions
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the ethics of the image
activities.name: atpEthicsSpot

config.prompt: This practice summary contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Media choice is clinical choice — a watercolour wash and a fine technical pen differ like a sedative and a stimulant.
Directive formats give containment and safety; open-studio freedom lets what emerges show itself.
Strong assessment documents outcomes against the goals set at intake.
Images may be shared on social media freely — consent applies only to selling them.
The artwork can reveal what clients did not intend to show, so image confidentiality is the ethical spine.
config.correction: Consent comes before display or social-media sharing — the artwork is confidential clinical material, enforced through the ATCB code and supervision.
config.why: The image can reveal what the client never meant to show; consent before display and restraint in interpretation are the profession's ethical spine.
